skill.name: vercel-react-best-practices
skill.description: Community skill that organizes React and Next.js performance guidance attributed to Vercel Engineering into agent-friendly rules for review and refactoring.
skill.summary: Agent-focused React and Next.js performance checklist for waterfalls, bundles, server data, and renders.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline code markers, reference URLs, and normal property names. No prompt injection, malicious command execution, secret handling, or data exfiltration behavior was found. One medium guidance concern remains because an inline hydration script example lacks explicit CSP and sanitization safeguards.

remediation.issue: Inline hydration script guidance lacks security guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note requiring static script bodies, no user-controlled interpolation, validated values, and CSP nonce compatibility before using dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

semantic_findings.title: Inline Hydration Script Guidance Lacks Safety Constraints
semantic_findings.description: The hydration rule presents an inline script through dangerouslySetInnerHTML as a correct pattern without warning about CSP nonces or untrusted interpolation. The shown script is static, but adapted versions could lead agents to generate unsafe inline scripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file clearly recommends an inline script pattern, but the example does not directly interpolate user input. The risk is guidance-level misuse when agents adapt the pattern.

content.value_statement: React and Next.js apps often suffer from waterfalls, large bundles, and wasted renders. This skill gives agents concrete Vercel performance rules for safer refactors.
actual_capabilities: Identifies async waterfalls and suggests Promise.all, Suspense, or dependency-based parallelization.
Guides bundle reductions with direct imports, dynamic loading, and intent-based preloading.
Reviews server-side React patterns, including RSC serialization, caching, and Next.js after().
Recommends SWR and shared subscriptions for client data fetching and global listeners.
Suggests re-render fixes such as functional state updates, derived subscriptions, and narrow effect dependencies.
Covers JavaScript and rendering optimizations for lists, SVGs, storage, regular expressions, and array work.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not benchmark, profile, or run tests by itself.
Examples must be adapted to the project framework, React version, and security policy.
Some rules trade faster paint for layout shift or more implementation complexity.
It does not replace official React, Next.js, or security documentation.

use_cases.title: Review Feature Performance
use_cases.description: Review a React feature for avoidable waterfalls, render churn, and expensive loops before merging.

use_cases.title: Refactor Server Routes
use_cases.description: Improve Next.js routes by streaming layouts, caching shared data, and shrinking RSC payloads.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Changes
use_cases.description: Ask an AI coding assistant to apply a prioritized performance checklist during UI refactors.

prompt_templates.title: Basic React Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component for the highest-impact performance issues from this skill. Focus on waterfalls, bundle size, and re-renders. Explain each fix in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Remove Route Waterfalls
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Next.js route to remove independent await waterfalls. Start independent operations early and use Suspense only where layout can stream safely.

prompt_templates.title: Audit App Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across server and client boundaries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature for RSC boundary serialization, client bundle growth, and repeated client fetches. Return a prioritized action plan with risks and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementations
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture decision for a larger workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare two implementations of this dashboard workflow against the skill rules. Recommend the version with better latency, bundle behavior, and render stability.

output_examples.input: A Next.js page waits for user, config, and sidebar data before rendering.
output: Starts independent requests at the page boundary.
Moves sidebar data into its own server component.
Adds a Suspense fallback only around slow content.
Lists tests for loading and error states.

output_examples.input: A React component imports icons from a package root and recreates filters during render.
output: Replaces package-root imports with direct icon imports or configured optimized imports.
Moves expensive derived values behind early loading returns.
Uses functional state updates for stable callbacks.

output_examples.input: A dashboard uses localStorage, cookies, and global key listeners.
output_examples.output: The review flags storage reads, listener duplication, and hydration tradeoffs. It recommends cache invalidation, shared subscriptions, and CSP-safe inline scripts.

best_practices: Start independent async work before awaiting dependent results.
Pass only client-used fields across server and client boundaries.
Document tradeoffs when a rule improves speed but changes loading behavior.
anti_patterns: Importing large libraries through barrel files without a Next.js optimization setting.
Moving every computation into memoization before checking early return paths.
Using inline hydration scripts without validating values or considering CSP.

faq.question: Does this skill run code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for an agent to apply while editing or reviewing code.

faq.question: Is it only for Next.js?
faq.answer: No. Many React and JavaScript rules apply outside Next.js, but server guidance is Next.js focused.

faq.question: Can it replace performance profiling?
faq.answer: No. Use profiling and bundle analysis to confirm changes on important paths.

faq.question: Does it require Vercel hosting?
faq.answer: No. Some notes mention Vercel features, but most rules are framework or runtime patterns.

faq.question: How should agents prioritize rules?
faq.answer: Start with async waterfalls and bundle size, then review server data, client fetching, and render churn.

faq.question: Are all examples safe to copy directly?
faq.answer: No. Adapt examples to your codebase, security policy, CSP, and library versions.
